newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzania's Nyerere sets date for Burundi talks.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania's Nyerere sets date for Burundi talks.

text.p: Tanzanian mediator on Burundi Julius Nyerere announced on Wednesday all-party talks aimed at resolving the country's civil war would start on August 25.
The talks would be the first public negotiations between the government of military leader Pierre Buyoya and the main Hutu rebel group the National Council for the Defence of Democracy (CNDD).
"Julius Nyerere hereby announces the date of 25th of August for the start of Burundi all-party talks at Arusha, Tanzania," said a statement from Nyerere's office.
The statement followed consultations between Nyerere's South Centre, special envoys to the Great Lakes region and protaganists in the conflict.
"Parties presently outside Burundi were also consulted," the statement said in a reference to CNDD.
Buyoya, who took power in a coup a year ago, signed a pre-ceasefire agreement with CNDD in April, after secret talks in Rome.

The agreement has not stopped the war in which more than 150,000 people have been killed since October 1993 when Tutsi troops murdered freely-elected Hutu President Melchior Ndadaye in an attempted coup.
Former Tanzanian president Nyerere was appointed last year international mediator on Burundi.
